normalized_claim: The organizing picture: a three-certificate loop: The results of this paper can be read as a minimal calculus for building hierarchical structure while keeping directionality honest. The core observation is that three notions often conflated in informal discussions are logically distinct and have distinct mathematical certificates: Stability / objects (completion). A theory level is specified by an idempotent endomap (exact or approximate); its fixed points are the “objects” at that theory level. In order theory this is a closure operator; in dynamics it is the induced endomap E_ tau,f . The certificate is (approximate) idempotence, quantified by the TV defect delta_ tau,f . Novelty / open-endedness (theory extension). Iterating a fixed completion rule saturates by idempotence. Strict ladder climbing therefore requires changing the theory/completion rule. The certificate is non-definability: a new predicate is not measurable with respect to the old partition-based theory. Our finite forcing lemma makes this generic: when there is hidden volume ( N-K>0 ), uniformly random predicate extensions are overwhelmingly non-definable. Directionality / irreversibility (audit). Arrow-of-time is defined on path space as Sigma_T(rho)=D_ KL ( P_ rho,T \|R_ * P_ rho,T ) . The certificate is either positive path-space KL or, under the accounted regime, a non-exact log-ratio 1-form (nonzero cycle affinities). Data processing ensures coarse-graining cannot create this certificate, and the protocol-trap theorem ensures it is not an artifact of hiding an internal clock.

normalized_claim: Role-projection alignment: Under honest bookkeeping and the witness discipline of Definition , each role projection is constrained as follows. [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] P1: admissible only when the candidate cluster carries a selected update, a quotient or relation record, and a witness of descent compatibility, descent obstruction, or update-vs-quotient mismatch. Generic semantics, generic predicate meaning, generic selection criteria, and generic agency are not admissible as P1 projections in the absence of such a witness. P2: admissible only when the candidate carries a macro specification, a realization relation, specification-satisfaction data, and evidence of representability or non-representability. Macro-level predicates or objectives count only insofar as they are treated as content to be represented. Mere quotient equality, arbitrary relations without representability structure, and empirical observations without level and threshold data are not admissible as P2 projections. P3: admissible only when the candidate carries enriched route grammar, generated same-source, same-target route terms, and route-comparison data with a non-reducibility or coherence-mismatch certificate. Generic transitions, generic causal arrows, generic path records, and route undefinedness arising from P1 obstruction are not admissible as P3 projections unless the route/coherence threshold is explicitly present and the route comparison is specifically of the P3 type. P4: admissible only when the candidate carries a stage, order, transition, refinement, staged-dynamics, or regime-ordering record with laws beyond bare labels. Bare labels, arbitrary relations without order, transition, or refinement law, quotient packaging, and audit bookkeeping are not admissible as P4 projections. P5: admissible only when the candidate carries a quotient relation, a packaging map, the identification of distinct micro-elements, a same-package or quotient-object record, and quotient-validity evidence. Generic structural paths, derivations, topologies or geometries merely because they have paths, and causal chains are not admissible as P5 projections unless quotient or packaging data is present. P6: admissible only when the candidate carries an audit record with event reference, provenance or dependency trace, replay or check structure, and bookkeeping or checkability structure. Passive logs alone, arbitrary metadata, and certificate-only content without audit/provenance/replay/check structure are not admissible as P6 projections. Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.alignment_rules); see Appendix .

Whether every finite audited feature is recognized — equivalently, whether the six roles are recognition-complete for FATCD — is left open and is recorded with the endogenous-instrument meta-limit of Sections and . normalized_claim: Promotion, SAU, and the boundary certificate.: Promotion is passage to a richer layer — C from R , ordinals from N , the 2 -adics from the odd integers — via a recorded bridge. The SAU pattern (Strict Audited Utility): a promoted object U that does not descend may still legally solve a lower-layer problem, provided a selected boundary expression C(U) does descend to a lower-layer answer; the audit never licenses treating U itself as a lower-layer object . Throughout this paper we call that descended, natively checkable assertion the boundary certificate — the term is this paper's own, introduced here once (the F-series papers use per-role certificate vocabulary instead), and it is used in a fixed sense: the native inequality, equality, or finite record that promoted support is allowed to purchase. Every Cluster A law is a SAU specialization in which the promoted object is temporal — a future-valuation ledger, an ordinal escrow, a potential — and the boundary certificate is a descent or termination statement; the 2 -adic ghost -1 of is the canonical non-descending promoted object.

normalized_claim: Methodology: eccentric problems as theorem detectors: This section has no counterpart in Foundations IV, and the addition is deliberate: the catalog's laws were not invented and then illustrated, they were mined, and the mining procedure is a first-class contribution of this paper. The raw material is the class of eccentric problems — Collatz, Goodstein, ErdH o s–Straus, Lychrel, Recam\'an, the angel problem, sandpiles, Langton's ant, Ducci, Gilbreath, aperiodic tilings, Hadwiger–Nelson, Apollonian packings — problems that are easy to state, resistant in a characteristic way, and each equipped with a folklore argument that everyone reaches for and that fails. The thesis of the method is that the folklore argument's failure is structured: what it illegitimately assumes is a promoted object, and what would repair it is a descended certificate, and the gap between the two, once it survives comparison against every existing law of the corpus, is a new law. For each problem, in order: Identify the tempting almost-proof — the argument everyone reaches for that fails. The almost-proof reveals the illegal overread. Name the promoted object the almost-proof secretly uses — an invariant measure on a completion, a fixed finite certificate package, a well-founded escrow. Typically the object does not descend to the native carrier. State what a lawful descended certificate would be. This fixes the boundary expression: the native, checkable assertion that promoted support is allowed to purchase ( ). Isolate the residual that survives every existing law. Run the candidate against the full Foundations IV catalog (exact statements, not summaries), the Foundations V laws, the nonclaim register, and the AOR status list. What remains unhandled is the law seed — and this step kills candidates as often as it produces them. Find the siblings. The seed is a law only if the same residual shape appears in at least three independent domains, at least one of them solved (the calibration instance). Otherwise it is a substrate observation, not a law. Admission then passes four further gates inherited from the corpus's discipline: a precise recognition source making every Setup datum definite; a rebadge test requiring the candidate to differ from every existing law on at least one declared axis — for all thirteen laws here the differentiating axis is the same, a step-indexed, growing, adversarial, or rate-comparison witness schema that no static catalog row possesses, which is why an editing pass that accidentally deletes a temporal quantifier from a law's statement collapses the law into its cousin and fails the gate; nonclaim compatibility (a law that needs an unconditional version of a forbidden inference is dead); and a replication ladder on the instantiation table (at least one solved calibration plus at least one instance with genuine engagement beyond citation). The remainder of this section runs the protocol on four seeds: two that became laws, and two that the protocol correctly killed.

normalized_claim: Conclusion: The central result of this paper is a closure theorem for typed audit carriers. Every carrier in PreSB_ S admits a completion into the audit-closed full subcategory through the reflection Cl_ SB . The construction does not merely adjoin missing data; it makes audit closure a structural operation, so that records, routes, residuals, statuses, nonclaims, and meta-audits remain visible as typed fields rather than being collapsed into an external well-formedness assertion. In that setting, the chain AOR^ ref ⊆AOR^ casc ⊆AOR organizes ordinary record-level audit closure, finite cascade closure, and closure stable under refinement limits. The framework comprises four layers. The first is the closure-completion reflection and its universal property. The second is the eight-stratum decomposition of the structural defect Xi_ SB , which turns failure of audit closure into typed diagnostic data. The third is the residual layer: the thirteen-type atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, together with the status catalogue, cost records, downstream obligations, and cascade graphs tracing how residual atoms are paid. The fourth is the refinement layer, where directed chains and asymptotic statuses distinguish finite discharge from discharge that only closes at a limit. Together they form a self-contained meta-theory of audit-closed carriers.

The principal positive case is reached when the native H6 strict domain closes, the strict test families on the new-layer carrier survive controls, and descent preserves old-layer compatibility without turning H2 into a strict-realized layer. Three weaker positive cases are reserved for incomplete new-layer evidence: a threshold-only case in which the new-layer readout slot is strict-realized but test-family reassembly is unavailable; a real-provisional case in which the route preserves or improves support without a completed threshold-and-slot gate; and a below-threshold or pending case. The same case analysis contains five blocking cases and two terminal negative cases. A blocker case obtains if promotion supplies no surviving object, if promotion survives but carrier exactification does not, if exactified threshold evidence cannot descend compatibly to the old layer, if source-policy admission blocks the source use, or if public-shadow safety blocks the route. A falsification case is legal only when neither old-layer nor new-layer threshold, readout, real-provisional, or below-threshold evidence remains. A separate implementation-failure case is reserved for malformed or unavailable artifacts, not for mathematical absence.

normalized_claim: Problem, result classes, and contribution map: Formal theories of consciousness are difficult to compare, and difficult to trust, partly because three different kinds of claim routinely travel in one sentence: mathematical claims about a formal structure, empirical claims about how that structure meets observation, and ontological claims about what the structure's satisfaction would be. The field has begun to treat this as a foundational problem rather than a stylistic one. General frameworks for mathematical models of consciousness ask what a model must declare before it says anything ; formal work on testability shows that inference procedures and prediction data can interact so badly that a theory becomes unfalsifiable or trivially falsified ; and large adversarial collaborations have demonstrated how much machinery is needed to test even two well-resourced theories against each other, without producing a definitive verdict . Landscape reviews count theory families by the dozen . In such a field, a paper's first obligation is to say exactly what kind of claim each of its sentences makes. This paper takes that obligation as its organizing principle. It presents an architecture for consciousness built from standard finite mathematics: finite carriers, lenses, quotients, refinements, closure operators, viability kernels, and audited promotion between description layers. Around that architecture it assembles a catalog of exact finite results, a small set of machine-checked kernels, and one explicitly priced ontological bridge. Every scientific sentence in the paper is assigned to one of four claim lanes, defined in Section : structural results [S] (theorems and exact finite constructions), recognition bridges [R] (proposed interpretive mappings, never derivations), ontological implications [O] (conditional on named postulates), and open targets [OPEN] . The lane discipline is not decoration; it is enforced by a sentence-level claim ledger in the artifact, and the paper's central negative rule is that no amount of [S] material ever implies an [O] conclusion without the named purchases.

normalized_claim: Why the criterion is layer-relative: Definition is intentionally stricter than merely being able to label states by zero and one. A candidate bit must remain stable long enough to matter, must support a descended operator calculus, and must survive audit. This is why the six primitives are complementary rather than redundant. P5 packages the carrier; P4 keeps it from dissolving immediately; P2 makes it semantically meaningful; P1 determines whether an effective operator vocabulary can be stabilized; P3 detects route dependence and protocol residue; P6 determines what must be paid to maintain the whole arrangement. The criterion is also intentionally broader than classical Booleanity. Complement and negation appear naturally when the relevant complements remain definable and stable at the lens. But nothing in Definition forces every layer to have those complements available at low cost. For that reason we speak of a logic layer rather than a Boolean layer. The finite laboratories studied in this paper are classical-looking enough to realize NOT, AND, and XOR cleanly, but the framework itself is meant to diagnose which closures a layer actually supports rather than to decree them in advance.
